Merged `main` (`983f527bd`) into `issue/2047-drag-to-rotate`. The new head is `405610b22`.

Files resolved by hand (both sides kept):
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: the hover call keeps the `frame_cost::time("ui/viewport.hover", ...)` timing from `main`. Inside it, the call keeps the hover gate of this PR (`left_press.is_some() || state.body_drag.is_some() || state.body_turn.is_some()`). The file keeps its CRLF line endings, as on `main`.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: the module list keeps `move_by` from this PR and `fixture_turn_ui` with `euler_deg` from `main`.

Git merged the other files without a conflict. I read the changes of `main` in `world.rs`, `lib.rs`, `mod.rs` and `tests.rs`. They do not change the same logic as this PR.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, `-j 6`): 17 steps, 0 failed, wall time 11.0 min. The steps include `ui suites: lib`.

Ready for a re-check (/resolve-conflicts check).

Quick pass (reads only, not built) of head 405610b229495163dbb29a5d6c7c268057355911.

Result: not ready.

Open points (fix before the ready flag):
- Point 2, Readings: the section names head 043b7e0a9 (ui lib: 1 failed). Update it to head 405610b22. The refresh comment reports 17 steps, 0 failed, on this head.
- Point 2, stack: the body says "Stacked on #1330", but the base is main. The diff includes the #1330 commits (crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs, crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs, docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md). Either set the base to the parent branch, or say that the merge waits for #1330.
- Point 8, Gate map: the new test files have no Gate map line: crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/body_drag.rs, crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/body_turn.rs, crates/ui/src/move_drag_tests.rs, crates/ui/src/turn_drag_tests.rs, crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_tests.rs.
- Point 8, layout: no structural.rs or page_layout.rs test names the new Move and Rotate buttons. Not confirmed.
- Point 7, line count: no file passes 400 lines for the first time. Four files already over 400 grow: shell.rs 1055 to 1076, state.rs 4768 to 4806, tests.rs 5152 to 5156, mod.rs 428 to 430. viewport_bar.rs goes from 433 to 419, still over 400.
- Point 3, MCP: no new app command. The new UI verbs MoveModelBy and TurnModelBy (crates/ui/src/state.rs) reach history through MoveModel. MCP move_model accepts a rotation (crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs). Reviewer to confirm that no MCP follow-up is owed.

Passed:
1. Head is 405610b22. GitHub reports MERGEABLE and CLEAN. The conflicts label is still set.
2. Body has what changed, readings, pinning tests, not exercised, a Changelog line and the issue reference line. Two before and after screenshots are linked (commit c75bf71a4). I did not open them.
3. Drag release goes through history.execute on MoveModel (crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs, place_part). It is one undo step.
4. No sys_ or raw world call in added lines.
5. No unwrap, expect or panic in added non-test lines. The expect calls sit in test files only.
6. No new file in crates/app/src. Each new file has a provenance line.
7. See the open point above.
8. No test is newly ignored or deleted. The two viewport bar tests moved to viewport_bar_tests.rs, which holds 3 tests.
9. No snapshot PNG, .github file, process file or new camcraft-* dependency in the diff. docs/decisions/2047-drag-to-rotate.md exists.
10. Safety floor: yes. The turn and move change part placement. Generated operations go stale, and the post refuses until a regenerate. Issue #2047 has effort:high.

Refresh of this PR after #1330 merged. The new head is `54ec20066`.

- Merge `3f1a72208` takes `origin/main` and keeps the two sides. Two files needed a hand resolve: `shell.rs` (the hover line of this PR, inside the frame-cost timing of main) and `move_drag.rs` (all of the centre cache of main is kept).
- The rotate drag now obeys the move-drag rules of #1330. It does not walk the facets in a still frame. It cancels on focus loss or pointer-gone. It holds at end-on and at the pivot, so it gives no NaN angle.
- New tests: `focus_loss_mid_turn_cancels_and_a_later_release_sends_no_turn`, `a_still_frame_walks_no_facets_and_a_turn_walks_them_again`, `a_cursor_on_the_pivot_holds_the_turn`.
- Quick gate on `54ec20066`: 17 steps, 0 failed (ui lib 1147 passed). Clippy on `camcraft-ui`: clean.

The PR stays a draft. The `conflicts` label is not changed by this refresh: the maintainer re-check decides it.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 54ec20066583716bd568add6dabe97c06ab44e72 -->
**Verdict: no blockers**

Full review of head `54ec20066`. Diff `origin/main...54ec20066` (merge base `bd0400ebb`), 15 files, +996 / -90. `git diff --stat` and `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat` are equal: no line-end change. A trial merge with the current `main` (`2f965f7d9`) is clean.

**Checks**
1. Everything is a command. The drag writes only `State::body_turn` (view state). `turn_drag::release` queues one `CommandKind::TurnModelBy`. The drain (`state_move_by.rs`, `turn_model_by` -> `place_part`) runs the one `MoveModel`, so the turn is one undo step. `body_turn::a_ring_drag_is_one_undoable_turn_that_stales_the_path_and_carries_the_stock` asserts: no world write and no history during the drag, one step at release, the post refuses with "regenerate", the stock holds the part, one undo restores the pose and the clean history. The preview turns only the shown vertices (`world.rs` `world_verts_by`). No new app command, so no new MCP tool. This follows the `MoveModelBy` precedent of #1330.
2. Never crash. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test lines. `plane_angle` refuses an end-on ray (`END_ON_SIN2`, NaN fails the comparison) before the division by `dn`. A hit within the hold radius of the pivot holds the angle. A zero-size pane gives no `aspect`, so no rings and `motion` returns early. The step is wrapped with `rem_euclid` to (-pi, pi], and a non-finite step is not added. `angle` is unwrapped, so more than one revolution counts. `turn_model_by` refuses a bad axis, a non-finite angle and a missing part by name. `document_target` checks that the result is finite. The `CenterCache` lock uses `PoisonError::into_inner`.
3. Frame cost. `turn_handles::draw` computes `rings_px` one time per frame and uses it for the paint and for the hot ring (`ring_in`). The centre comes from the shared `shown_center` cache. The cache key is entity, facet `Arc` and pose bits, so a Move and a Rotate of the same part share one entry and a pose change makes it new. During a turn, `rings` uses the press centre and does not ask the cache. The counter test is real: ten still frames keep `computes` constant, a turn adds one walk, and the next frame adds none.
4. Cancel and mode interplay. Escape is consumed only while a drag is live, and it cancels the two drags. Focus loss and `PointerGone` cancel the turn, and a later release queues nothing (test). A ring press does not set `left_press`, so the drag does not orbit (`state.drag == None` is asserted). A press off the rings still orbits (test). Move and Rotate are mutually exclusive, and each toggle cancels the two drags (`viewport_bar_tests::move_and_rotate_modes_never_share_the_part`).
5. The merge. `git show --remerge-diff 3f1a72208` shows two hand resolves only. `shell.rs`: the `update_hover` line keeps the `frame_cost` timing of main and adds `state.body_turn.is_some()`. `move_drag.rs`: all of `CenterCache`, `pose_bits` and the cached `shown_center` of main are kept, and `shown_center` becomes `pub(crate)`. The focus-loss cancel of #1330 is kept and extended.
6. Layers. All new code is in `crates/ui`. No `sys_*` or raw world call in the UI files. No component is declared outside `schema.rs`.
7. Tests. 17 `#[test]` lines added, 2 removed (the two bar tests moved unchanged to `viewport_bar_tests.rs`). No test is deleted or ignored. No snapshot PNG. Each new test file has a provenance line and a Gate map line.
8. Text and assets. "Rotate: drag a ring on the selected part", "Turn about Z: +35.0°" and "turned Block +20.0° about Z" are plain English. The Rotate glyph is painted in code; there is no new icon file. The body has before and after screenshots (both files exist at `c75bf71a4`), a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2047`. The decision file has the `## #N - <title>` format with decided, why, dropped and cost to change.

**Non-blocking findings**
- `turn_drag.rs` `ring_hit`: the press angle `ring_phi` comes from the index `k` in the filtered polyline. When a ring point is behind the camera, `rings_px` drops it, and `k` no longer gives the true angle. The value is used only when `plane_angle` fails at the press. A wrong start angle can then make the first motion jump. Recommend: keep the angle with each projected point.
- A ring that is within 3 degrees of end-on can be grabbed (the cursor shows Grab and the ring is drawn hot), but every motion holds, so the drag never turns the part. Recommend: do not offer the hit for an end-on ring, or dim it.
- `turn_drag::release`: a drag of exactly one full turn (angle near 2*pi) passes `MIN_TURN_RAD` and makes a history step with no visible change. Recommend: compare the angle modulo 2*pi with the limit.
- The preview pivot is the centre at press (`TurnDrag::center`). The drain uses `shown_center` at release (`document_target`). The two are equal unless the pose changes during the drag (for example Ctrl+Z with the button down). Then the release turns the new pose about a different centre than the preview showed. Recommend: carry the press centre in `TurnModelBy`, or cancel the turn when the pose changes.
- MCP: there is no MCP verb for "turn about the bounding-box centre by an angle". An agent can set the rotation with `move_model`, but it must compute the pivot itself. Same gap as `MoveModelBy`. A `P7` follow-up `MCP: turn a part about its centre` is optional.
- Layout: no `page_layout.rs` or `structural.rs` test names the Rotate button. The bar buttons are painted and have no AccessKit node (this is the same for all bar buttons before this PR). `bar_fits_its_buttons` covers the new count.
- File lengths: `viewport_bar.rs` goes from 461 to 419 lines (better, still over 400). `shell.rs` and `state.rs` grow; the `shell.rs` split is held by #2508.
- The `conflicts` label is still set, but the PR merges cleanly with the current `main`. The maintainer re-check can remove it.
